leadText:
]]
This page details characters who own a first partner Pokémon in different media throughout the franchise.

==In the manga==
===Pokémon Adventures===
In Pokémon Adventures, the first partner Pokémon featured in the games are reserved for the few people who hold a Pokédex. produces three Pokédexes for each region, and gives out the three first partner Pokémon in each region along with the Pokédex to Trainers he thinks are talented. He has colleagues and friends like Professor Birch do this for him in regions in which he isn't present. In the Unova region, two sets of first partner Pokémon are given out to six Trainers, but still with only three Pokédexes. Professor Oak also gave Red's Pikachu as a special first partner to .

===Pokémon animated series===
During , caught all but two of the first partner Pokémon: , , , , , and . The Grass-type first partner from Kalos, , is instead owned by , and the Grass-type first partner from Galar, , is instead owned by Goh.
Every first partner Pokémon obtained by a main character has evolved at least once.
Each first partner Pokémon obtained by a main character was not battled: 's , , and chose to join his team, while Ash fought and won against Misty for his . Brock's chose to join him. May received her from Professor Oak, Dawn received her from Professor Rowan, Lana rescued her from Team Skull, and Goh caught his without battling it. Although she is not a main character, Dot’s chose to join her team as her first Pokémon.
The Kanto first partner set is the only full first partner set that has obtained where every member was owned by a previous Trainer.
Conversely, the Johto first partner set is the only full first partner set that Ash has obtained where none of the members were previously owned by another Trainer or a Pokémon Professor, as all of them were caught in the wild.
The Hoenn first partner set is the first set in which all three Pokémon evolve under the care of the main characters who own them.

Every first partner Pokémon obtained by a main character has evolved at least once.
Each first partner Pokémon obtained by a main character was not battled: 's , , and chose to join his team, while Ash fought and won against Misty for his . Brock's chose to join him. May received her from Professor Oak, Dawn received her from Professor Rowan, Lana rescued her from Team Skull, and Goh caught his without battling it. Although she is not a main character, Dot’s chose to join her team as her first Pokémon.
The Kanto first partner set is the only full first partner set that has obtained where every member was owned by a previous Trainer.
Conversely, the Johto first partner set is the only full first partner set that Ash has obtained where none of the members were previously owned by another Trainer or a Pokémon Professor, as all of them were caught in the wild.
The Hoenn first partner set is the first set in which all three Pokémon evolve under the care of the main characters who own them.
As 's was revealed to be under his ownership before his , it caused many to hearken back to , where the player starts with , like , and the rival starts with Eevee. This was disproven when Gary finally revealed his Blastoise to Ash.

The first partner Pokémon of each region that are given to characters based on the male protagonists in the games cycle through ( , , and ), ( , , and ), and ( and ). The pattern was broken with , who has a Grass-type first partner Pokémon instead of the expected Water-type first partner Pokémon, however it has continued with , who has a Fire-type first partner Pokémon.
This also applies to characters based on the female protagonists in the games, which cycle through Water ( , , and ), Grass ( , , and ), and Fire ( , , and ). The pattern was broken with , who has a Grass-type first partner Pokémon instead of the expected Water-type first partner Pokémon.
The first partner Pokémon of the characters based on the male protagonists usually have the type advantage over the characters based on the female protagonists, with the only exception of the main characters of the where has the type advantage over .
